_readme: Named characters. The key (e.g. "mira") is her id; keep it lowercase with no spaces.

role: house (comes with a house; the house in js/data/economy.js names her as npc), partner (starter choice, later shows up looking for work), story (joins through a house story), guild (Adventurers Guild), drifter (no strings: turns up among candidates now and then). Crossover guests live in data/guests.json instead.

name is her actual name only (first + family name, as she would be addressed by friends). title (optional) is an honorific or rank like Lady, Dame, Captain, Professor or Princess: shown in front of her name on cards and her sheet (titled(w)) and given to the AI as {title}/{fullname}, but never part of the name. It is a title from data/titles.json (its label or id), so it carries that title's perk; she can earn more in play.

personality must match a key in personalities.json. traits from the trait list (Shy, Eager, Ambitious, Party Animal, Former Adventurer, Elegant, Lazy, Tough, Romantic, Greedy, Loyal, Exhibitionist, Night Owl, Modest).
fav / dislike / lovers: service ids from services.json (lovers = what she enjoys only with Sam once she is his lover), or null.
partnerTrust / partnerLewd / partnerStory: only for partners. backstory is shown on her sheet.
design: appearance used for image prompts. under/underColor: undergarments id (plain, lace, silk, sports, corset, sheer, none) and color.
outfits: sig_<key> is her starting outfit; sp_<key> unlocks at trust 60 or as a lover. prompt is the image wording; bonus multiplies income for jobs or client classes.
Partners only get a romance story if one exists in js/stories/partners.js; without one they still work, just without the arc.

bonds: optional starting bonds with other named ladies: {"otherKey": {"v": 40, "kind": "mentor", "note": "..."}}. v from -100 (rivals) to 100. kind: mentor (she mentors them), home (both from Sam's old world), comrades. See bonds.json.

keepOn: optional {"item": "...", "trust": 90, "aside": true}. Until her trust reaches that, image prompts keep the item on; with aside the rest of her clothes only get pulled aside (js/logic/prompts.js keepOnRule). outfits.sp_<key>.unlock: optional trust needed for her special outfit instead of 60 (being a lover doesn't bypass it).

jobs: {likes:[...], dislikes:[...]} job ids she enjoys / would rather not do (mood each week, and she takes liked jobs at any trust). Ladies without it roll their own from personality and traits (balance.json → jobPrefs).
ngplus: partners only. true = she only appears as a partner choice from New Game+ (cycle 2), and not in the first cycle's partner list. Cycle-1 partners leave it out.
vignettes: partners only. [{title, text, trust}] short slice-of-life 'Moments' on her sheet, each unlocked when her trust with Sam reaches that number.

unique: {name, desc, fx} her personal semi-unique trait. fx uses only the effect keys from docs/OVERHAUL.md section 2 (maxEnergy, actQuality, jobBonus, security, energyBank, ...). Service ids: kiss, massage_give, massage_get, manual_give, manual_get, oral_give, oral_get, breast_give, breast_get, missionary, cowgirl, doggy (old ids manual/oral/paizuri/caress still work). fav/lovers can be a receiving service (*_get): she likes being on the other end.

body: {bust: flat|small|medium|large|huge, height: short|average|tall, figure: slim|athletic|curvy|soft}. Used for image wording and body effects (docs/OVERHAUL.md section 3). Job ids are courtesan, madame, promoter, maid, bartender, attendant, dancer, bath, security.

mira.name: Mira Ashdown
mira.backstory: Mira kept the Gilded Lantern running for the old owner until he vanished. She isn't sure what to make of the skinny stranger with the deed, but she's staying. For now. She knows every regular by name and every creaky floorboard by sound, and she has quietly started mothering the man who inherited it all.

design.features: a beauty mark beside her lips

tsubaki.name: Tsubaki
tsubaki.backstory: Tsubaki came from the eastern isles to run the springs for her late aunt. She knows every guest's name and every guest's bath temperature. Her aunt's wooden bath bucket sits by the door for luck, and she sings off-key, loudly, to whoever is in the water.

vesper.title: Lady
vesper.name: Vesper
vesper.backstory: Vesper has haunted the manor for three centuries and was delighted to finally have company. She doesn't remember how she died and finds the question rude. She greets every arrival in a gown of her own era, and her ideas of hospitality are three hundred years out of date and perfectly charming.

hilde.name: Hilde Ironsong
hilde.backstory: A brewmaster who lost her brewery in a drinking contest with a giant. She wants a bar to run and doesn't much care what goes on upstairs, though she's not opposed to finding out. She still swears the giant cheated, keeps a barrel of the bet's vintage under the counter and offers a free pint to anyone who can out-drink her. Nobody has.

sylphine.name: Sylphine Moonwhisper
sylphine.backstory: A dancer who left the elven conservatory to perform for "people who actually clap." She treats every night at the Pavilion like opening night. After a century of precision and polite silence she lives for the roar of an audience, and can be talked into almost anything by applause.

design.features: silver anklets and a crescent-moon tattoo on her hip

zaria.name: Zaria Nightbloom
zaria.backstory: Zaria ran the Veil's floor long before the deed changed hands. She thinks humans are adorable and Sam is the most adorable one yet. For decades she has handled the house's difficult clients with a smile and a velvet rope, and she quietly keeps a ledger of the favors people owe her.

bettina.name: Bettina Krumm
bettina.backstory: Bettina has run the Wayfarer's front desk for a decade. She can tell where a traveler is from by their boots and how much they'll spend by their hat. She keeps a drawer of lost-and-found trinkets and a surprisingly kind heart behind her tally book.

design.hairStyle: honey-brown hair in a practical bun

kaede.name: Kaede
kaede.backstory: Kaede was the scout of a four-person party called the Copper Foxes until a collapsing dungeon floor and a leader who ran first ended it. Pride kept her from going home empty-handed, so she took a room at the Lantern "for a week" and found she was good at watching doors. She has never been anyone's guard before, and has never been anyone's friend for free either.
kaede.partnerStory: In his first hour in this world Sam stumbled into a goblin ambush and, almost entirely by accident, shoved a fox-eared scout out of the path of a crossbow bolt. Nobody had ever put themselves in front of Kaede before. She keeps a running tally of favors in her head, Sam is hopelessly in the red, and she has decided the only fair repayment is staying close. She has also decided he's cute.

design.features: a thin scar on her shoulder

sig_kaede.label: Adventurer's leathers
sig_kaede.prompt: a fitted leather vest, wrap skirt and arm guards

sp_kaede.label: Shrine maiden garb
sp_kaede.prompt: a red and white shrine maiden outfit with detached sleeves

unique.name: Fox's Instinct
unique.desc: She hears trouble before it starts and is quick to step in.

vignettes.title: The Ledger
vignettes.text: Kaede keeps a tally of what she owes Sam on the backs of bar receipts. One rescue. Two dinners. One very good bandage. She slaps the stack down in front of him and announces she'll be settling up "eventually." When Sam says she doesn't owe him anything, she gives him a long look, crosses out RESCUE, and writes IDIOT in its place. Then she tucks the receipts back into her vest like treasure and doesn't mention them again, except to ask, a week later, whether he has any more dinners she should be paying for.

vignettes.title: Tail Etiquette
vignettes.text: Over breakfast Kaede explains the rules: nobody touches the tail without being invited, a low swish means leave me alone, a fluffed tip means she's been startled and will deny it. Sam nods seriously. Halfway through the lesson he realizes that her tail has been curled around his chair leg the entire time. She notices him noticing. "That's an accident," she says, and does not move it. They finish the eggs in a silence that is much louder than their usual one.

vignettes.title: Night Watch
vignettes.text: Kaede sits on the roof by the chimney every night after close, watching the street. Sam climbs up with two bowls of soup and a blanket he has no intention of using himself. She tells him about the Foxes: the leader who ran, the friend who didn't make it out, the way she learned to trust nobody who couldn't carry their own weight. "You can't," she says, looking at his soup-spilling hands. "And I still trust you." She shifts over to share the blanket without being asked.

vignettes.title: The Badge
vignettes.text: Kaede pulls a dented copper badge from her pack, the crest of the Copper Foxes, and turns it over in her fingers. "Kept it for years. Thought I'd go back and throw it in the leader's face." She presses it into Sam's palm instead. "I don't need it anymore. I've got a new party, and it's a terrible one. Skinny leader. Zero combat skills. No loot." Her ears are flat with embarrassment; her tail is wrapped all the way around his wrist.

yui.name: Yui Mori
yui.backstory: Yui spent six years in the accounts department of a mid-sized firm, two desks from Sam, keeping everyone's numbers honest and her own feelings filed under "later." She woke up in Hollowmere a week before him with a stapler in her pocket and no explanation, and spent that week learning the local coins and discovering that nobody here had ever invented the spreadsheet. She gets inexplicably emotional about instant noodles.
yui.partnerStory: Yui sat at the next desk over in Sam's old office, and was crossing the same street when the truck came. She woke in this world a week before him, and when a familiar hoodie turned up in the Lantern's doorway she nearly dropped the account book. She's been quietly reorganizing Sam's finances ever since, which is what she does when she's nervous. And happy. And both.

design.features: thin-framed glasses and a nervous habit of pushing them up

sig_yui.label: Office clothes from Earth
sig_yui.prompt: a white button-up blouse, grey pencil skirt, black tights and thin-framed glasses

sp_yui.label: Adventurer "cosplay"
sp_yui.prompt: a deliberately cliché fantasy adventurer outfit with a short cape and thigh-high boots

unique.name: Spreadsheet Wizardry
unique.desc: She turns the house's numbers into a quiet advantage.

vignettes.title: Borrowed Stapler
vignettes.text: Yui sets a battered office stapler on the ledger desk like it's a holy relic. "It was in my pocket when I woke up," she says. "I don't know why." Sam picks it up and finds his own initials scratched into the base: he lent it to her three years ago and never asked for it back. They stare at it for a long time. Then Yui starts laughing, the helpless kind, and Sam joins in, and neither of them can quite explain to the passing maid what is so funny about a stapler.

vignettes.title: Color Code
vignettes.text: Sam's week arrives on his desk color-coded: blue for appointments, green for payments, a cheerful yellow for "things you'll forget." Yui pushes her glasses up and admits she did this at the old office too, quietly covering his deadlines in a tab no one else could see. "I never told you." "I knew," Sam says, which is a lie. She narrows her eyes. He amends it to "I suspected." She hands him a pink sheet. Pink, she explains, is for things she'd like to do with him, and it is currently blank.

vignettes.title: Quarter-End
vignettes.text: Closing the books at midnight feels exactly like the old quarter-end rush: bad lighting, worse tea, the two of them hunched over numbers. Yui props her chin on her hand and watches Sam work instead of working herself. "I stayed late on purpose, you know. Back then. Every time." She says it very casually, to the ledger. Sam sets his pen down. The lamp hums. "I'm not staying late for the books tonight, either," she adds, and finally looks up, pink to the ears.

vignettes.title: Spare Key
vignettes.text: Yui presses a small brass key into Sam's hand: the ledger room, her room, her whole carefully ordered kingdom. "I want you to know where everything is. In case I'm ever not here." Sam starts to protest, and she shakes her head. "I woke up alone for a week, Sam. I'm not saying I'm going anywhere. I'm saying I'd like to be someone who trusts people with the key." He closes his fingers around it. She straightens her glasses, then takes them off entirely, which is the bravest thing he has ever seen her do.

nerys.name: Nerys
nerys.backstory: Nerys has spent two centuries writing contracts for other people's desires while carefully never wanting anything herself. The summoning that went wrong was supposed to be her last job before "retiring" to a villa on the southern coast. She tells everyone she is between contracts. The truth is she hasn't had a place that was hers in decades, and she is absolutely not lonely.
nerys.partnerStory: Nerys was mid-summoning when Sam fell out of the sky and landed in her circle. The contract bound itself to him instead, through a clause she wrote herself and has never once seen trigger. She is furious. She reads the fine print every night looking for a loophole, and has so far only discovered that she doesn't want one.

design.features: small bat wings, curled horns and a slender tail

sig_nerys.label: Succubus attire
sig_nerys.prompt: a black leather corset, thigh-high boots and long gloves

sp_nerys.label: "Disguise": librarian
sp_nerys.prompt: a prim high-collared librarian dress and glasses, barely hiding her horns

unique.name: Contract Clause
unique.desc: A fine-print mind that sweetens her service and draws admirers.

vignettes.title: Fine Print
vignettes.text: Nerys slaps a scroll on the lounge table, annotated in red. "Clause nine. The summoner shall feed the demon. You, Sam, have been in breach for three days." Sam checks the clause. It does say that. The next one covers dessert. He brings her a slice of berry pie, and she eats it with the offended dignity of a queen accepting tribute. "Acceptable. Clause ten is about compliments." She waits. He gives her one. She refuses to react, but her tail has curled into a heart shape and she either doesn't know or doesn't care.

vignettes.title: Sore Wings
vignettes.text: Sam notices Nerys has been sleeping in the lounge chair, wings folded stiff, wincing every time she stretches. Her bed is too narrow for them; she'd rather suffer than ask. By morning there's a custom-built pillow stack on her mattress and a hand-sewn wing cushion. "This is extortion," she informs him. "You're buying my loyalty with comfort." She sleeps in the bed that night, and for the first time in weeks she's visibly rested. When Sam mentions it she tells him that was never in doubt, and also thank you, but quieter.

vignettes.title: The Villa
vignettes.text: Nerys unrolls a faded sketch: a villa on a cliff, a garden of night-blooming flowers, a long balcony. She planned it for decades. "Retirement," she says. Sam studies the drawing and notices that the balcony has two chairs. One is smudged where the ink was erased and redrawn. "For guests," she says, too quickly. "People retire with furniture. That's all." He doesn't push. He just sets his finger beside the second chair, and she lets him leave it there.

vignettes.title: Clause Zero
vignettes.text: Late at night Nerys confesses that every contract she's ever written contains a hidden "Clause Zero": the demon may leave at any time, no penalty. "Nobody ever read that far," she says. "I wrote it so I'd always have a way out. I've never used it." She turns the scroll over. Sam's contract has the clause too, in her tidy hand. Beneath it, newly scratched out, are three words she tried to write and couldn't. She tears the corner off. "Don't read the fine print," she tells him, and kisses him so he won't ask.

elowen.name: Elowen Dawnleaf
elowen.backstory: Elowen left the cedar glade of her people with a satchel of herbs, a letter of introduction to a human physician who turned out to have died six years earlier, and no plan at all. She learned the rest from dock injuries and market-day fevers. Elves live long, and she has been quietly lonely for most of hers; patients are the nearest thing to company she has allowed herself.
elowen.partnerStory: Elowen found Sam unconscious on the road after his arrival, burning with a fever no herbal book listed, and nursed him for three days. She still checks his temperature when he looks pale. Lately she checks it when he doesn't, as an excuse to stand close. She has not noticed how many excuses she has.

design.features: freckles and a sprig of rosemary in her braid

sig_elowen.label: Healer's robes
sig_elowen.prompt: soft white healer's robes with green embroidery and a satchel of herbs

sp_elowen.label: Forest silk dress
sp_elowen.prompt: a light leaf-green silk dress woven with tiny flowers

unique.name: Healer's Touch
unique.desc: Her massages restore the body, and she recovers a little faster herself.

vignettes.title: Tea Notes
vignettes.text: Elowen keeps a little notebook of what tea suits whom. Sam's page, when he sneaks a look, reads: "Chamomile: tired. Peppermint: pretending not to be. Ginger: worrying about money. Honey: he doesn't know he needs this." He's made the honey list longer without noticing. When she catches him reading she snatches the book to her chest and goes pink from collarbone to ear tip. "It's for medicine," she says. He agrees that it is. They both drink the honey tea anyway.

vignettes.title: Dock Hours
vignettes.text: Sam watches Elowen kneel on the wet dock treating a stevedore's torn hand, her voice low and sure, her fingers steady. The big man hardly flinches. When she ties off the bandage he thanks her gruffly and she tells him he's welcome, perfectly poised, until Sam says she's amazing and she drops the roll of linen in the harbor. "I'm only a healer," she mumbles, fishing it out. "Only," Sam repeats. She walks home three steps ahead of him so he can't see her smile.

vignettes.title: Long Springs
vignettes.text: On the roof, Elowen tells Sam she once counted: a human life is about seventy years. "To my people that's one long spring." Sam, who has been carefully not thinking about this, goes quiet. She takes his hand. "Don't be sad. I'd rather have one spring than no season at all." She picks a petal from the potted flower she'd smuggled up and tucks it behind his ear. "There. Now it's spring." It is not the right season, but he lets her pretend.

vignettes.title: A Letter Home
vignettes.text: For the first time in years Elowen is writing to her glade. She reads Sam a draft: it begins with the dock and the herbs and the tiresome stairs at the Lantern, and ends with a line that makes her hand shake on the page. "I am not far from home anymore." She doesn't ask Sam what he thinks. She seals the letter with her own wax and hands it to him to post, a gesture that, among her people, means "I trust you with who I am." He holds it carefully, like something alive.

adelheid.title: Dame
adelheid.name: Adelheid Valk
adelheid.backstory: Dame Adelheid took her vows at twenty-two and has spent the years since being her chapter's example of what a knight should be. She has guarded relics, escorted bishops and read the foretelling of the hero so many times she can recite it. It says nothing about what the hero eats for breakfast, which she has since discovered she cares about intensely. The romance novels hidden in her saddlebag are the only place she lets a knight get what she wants.
adelheid.partnerStory: When the Radiant Order foretold a hero from another world, Adelheid swore her sword and life to him before he ever arrived. Then a tired man in a hoodie fell out of the sky holding the deed to a pleasure house, and she had to reconcile prophecy with reality. She takes her oath extremely seriously. Sam would like her to take it slightly less seriously, and privately, so would she.

design.features: a scar through one eyebrow

sig_adelheid.label: Retainer's half-plate
sig_adelheid.prompt: polished silver half-plate armor over a blue tabard bearing a sun crest

sp_adelheid.label: Off-duty doublet
sp_adelheid.prompt: a fitted navy doublet, white shirt open at the collar, and riding boots

nerys.note: A holy knight and a demon who both claim Sam. It goes about how you'd expect.

unique.name: Oath of the Order
unique.desc: A knight's discipline: hard to rattle and hard to get past.

vignettes.title: Relics of the Hero
vignettes.text: Adelheid has been cataloguing Sam's belongings in a leather-bound inventory titled RELICS OF THE HERO. Entry one: a hooded garment of unknown weave. Entry two: a small metal talisman on a ring. Sam points out that the talisman is a convenience-store keychain. She writes that down too, reverently, and adds a margin note: "Remarkably well-preserved." He tries to keep a straight face. She, to her credit, nearly manages it herself, until the corner of her mouth betrays her and the page gets a small, dignified blot.

vignettes.title: Dawn Drill
vignettes.text: Adelheid wakes Sam at dawn for sword practice. He is terrible. She corrects his stance for the fortieth time, hands settling on his shoulders, and then says gravely that his form is "improving." It is not. They both know it is not. She says it anyway, and a look crosses her face that she hurries to cover with a lecture about footwork. At the end of the hour she presses a clean towel into his hands with a stiff little bow, and lingers at the training-yard gate until he's inside.

vignettes.title: The Third Book
vignettes.text: Caught again with a novel, Adelheid decides honor requires a full confession. She reads Sam a passage aloud, deadpan: a knight kneels before her lord, who raises her to her feet. Her voice stays level through the first paragraph. By the second she is reading slower. By the third she stops mid-sentence and stares at the page as if it had betrayed her. "It is only fiction," she says. Sam takes the book gently from her hands and reads the next line aloud himself. She does not stop him.

vignettes.title: Out of Armor
vignettes.text: At dusk Adelheid sits in the yard polishing her breastplate piece by piece, and tonight, for the first time, she has set aside the rest of it too: the gauntlets, the greaves, even the formal tabard. She is just a woman in a linen shirt with nicks and scars on her hands. "I have never been unarmored in front of anyone I wasn't guarding," she says. Sam sits down beside her without speaking. After a while she leans, very slightly, until her shoulder meets his. Neither of them is guarding anything.

natsuki.name: Natsuki Hayama
natsuki.backstory: Natsuki grew up three doors down from Sam and, by her own count, won every race, argument and eating contest between them. One evening three years ago she took a shortcut and walked out of an alley into a forest in another world. With no map, no language she could read, and nobody who knew her name, she took the first job anyone offered: carrying a sword for a caravan. She has been swinging it ever since, and has never stopped missing the sound of someone calling her "Natsu."
natsuki.partnerStory: Natsuki was Sam's childhood friend back home. She vanished three years ago and nobody ever found her. Turns out she's been here the whole time, carving out a name as an adventurer. She cried when she saw him. Then she punched him. Then she cried harder, and now she follows him around the Lantern claiming it's "for the free meals."

design.features: a sticking plaster on her cheek and a confident grin

sig_natsuki.label: Veteran adventurer gear
sig_natsuki.prompt: a worn blue scarf, fitted leather armor and a katana at her hip

sp_natsuki.label: Summer festival yukata
sp_natsuki.prompt: a bright orange summer festival yukata with a goldfish pattern

akari.note: Natsuki knew Akari back home as her friend Kenta's younger sister.

kaede.note: Two adventurers, one guard post, and a lot of opinions about swordwork.

unique.name: Bottomless Appetite
unique.desc: She eats like a horse and recovers like one too.

vignettes.title: Scoreboard
vignettes.text: Natsuki produces a crumpled sheet of paper from her pack: a tally of every contest she and Sam ever had, from races to staring matches. It's 214 to 213, in her favor. "I kept it going in my head for three years," she says, scowling at the floor. "Seemed wrong to let you catch up while I wasn't there." Sam asks what the final contest was. "Eating," she says. "You lost badly. You always lose badly." He suggests a rematch. Her face does something complicated, and then she cracks her knuckles.

vignettes.title: Mochi Disaster
vignettes.text: Natsuki is determined to recreate the mochi her grandmother made. The local rice is wrong, the pounding mallet is too big, and by the end of the afternoon the kitchen ceiling has a sticky white handprint on it that nobody can reach. She stands in the wreckage, dusted white, looking about twelve seconds from tears or a sword. Sam tastes the one piece that survived. It is lumpy and bland and perfect. "Liar," she says, wiping her eyes with a floury wrist. She eats the rest standing very close to him.

vignettes.title: Scabbard Marks
vignettes.text: Natsuki shows Sam the scabbard of her sword. Along the underside are small neat notches in rows of seven: one for every week since she arrived. She never says out loud that she was counting, but the scabbard is nearly full. The latest row is shorter than the rest, and fresh. "I stopped counting," she admits. "The day you showed up. Didn't need to anymore." She tucks the sword back at her hip, looks at the ceiling, and asks whether there's any food left. There always is.

vignettes.title: Festival Song
vignettes.text: Late at night, on the town wall, Natsuki starts humming a melody from the summer festivals of home. Sam knows it. He hums the second line, and she falls silent, then takes the next one a little too fast, and they carry it to the end in two unsteady voices. When the song is over she doesn't say anything. She just puts her head on his shoulder like she has done a thousand times, and he can feel her shaking with laughter or something else. Neither of them says which.

kanako.name: Kanako Ishida
kanako.backstory: Kanako worked nine years in a small snack bar where she was the hostess, the confidante and the bouncer, and she can tell by the sound of the door how a man's evening has gone. In this world she walked into the first drink stall she found and has been teaching bartenders to listen ever since. Her laugh is the loudest thing in any room, which is how she likes it: a loud laugh means nobody has to know when she's lonely.
kanako.partnerStory: Kanako lived in the apartment next door to Sam for six years. She fed him when he forgot to eat, taught him to sort the recycling and teased him mercilessly. He had a hopeless crush on her the entire time; she thought of him as the neighbor who would never learn to cook. The truck, it turns out, was very efficient: now she's in a world where nobody else knows how she takes her coffee, and the only person who does is the one she keeps calling "Sammy."

design.features: a beauty mark under her left eye and red lipstick

sig_kanako.label: Snack-bar mama outfit
sig_kanako.prompt: a fitted wine-red cocktail dress with a cardigan over her shoulders

sp_kanako.label: Date-night dress
sp_kanako.prompt: a sleek black off-shoulder dress she bought "just in case"

unique.name: Snack-Bar Mama
unique.desc: A hostess who can read a room and a man's mood from the doorway. Hosting comes naturally.

vignettes.title: Tupperware
vignettes.text: A covered bowl turns up on Sam's desk with a sticky note in handwriting he'd know anywhere: "EAT. -K." Inside is something that is trying very hard to be miso stew, with local vegetables in all the wrong places. He eats it all, standing up, and it is exactly like six years of tupperware left outside his apartment door. When he brings the empty bowl back to the bar, Kanako takes it without looking at him and says, "Don't make that face." He wasn't making a face. She was.

vignettes.title: Last Train
vignettes.text: Kanako reminisces, wiping a glass: the nights she'd come home at two in the morning, shoes in her hand, and find Sam's light still on next door. "I used to tap the wall twice," she says, "and you'd tap back, even half asleep. I never told you why." Sam asks why. She puts the glass down, shrugs, and says it was so she'd know someone was home. The bar is empty, and the quiet that follows is her kind of quiet, soft and a little shy.

vignettes.title: Reading the Room
vignettes.text: Kanako runs a "listening lesson" for the bar staff, with Sam as her volunteer. Don't fill the silence, she says. Watch hands, not mouths. Ask the second question, not the first. Halfway through she realizes she is describing herself, and that he is looking at her the way she'd teach someone to look at a person who needs to be heard. She loses her place in the lesson. The staff discreetly find urgent reasons to be elsewhere. Kanako laughs it off, loudly, then admits it was a good lesson.

vignettes.title: The Chime
vignettes.text: Kanako has hung a small brass chime over the bar door, the same as the one at her old snack bar. "I could always tell who came in by the sound," she says. "Drunks, regulars, trouble." She turns to Sam. "And you. I knew your footsteps in the hallway for six years, Sam. I knew when you were sad. I knew when you'd stopped eating." The chime rings softly in the draft. "I just didn't know what to call it. I think I do now." She sets down the glass, and doesn't tease him at all.

akari.name: Akari Kurosawa
akari.backstory: Akari Kurosawa is Kenta's younger sister, and for most of her adult life she has been the person at the edge of Sam and Kenta's evenings: the one who brought the snacks, stole the controller and walked Sam to the station when he missed the last train. Sam was kind to her in small, unshowy ways. He remembered her favorite flavor, listened to her bad-boss stories and never once teased her about a crush everyone else could see. In this world nobody is watching, and she has no intention of wasting it.
akari.partnerStory: Akari is the younger sister of Sam's best friend Kenta, and she has had a crush on him for years, through game nights, bad bosses and one catastrophic haircut. She tagged along to the crosswalk that day, by her own account "just walking by," carrying a spare umbrella she had decided would make a good excuse. Kenta had stopped to tie his shoe, and she holds onto the thought that he's fine. Sam is the one familiar face in a very strange world, and Akari has decided that this is fate, and that it's time to stop being "Kenta's sister."

design.hairStyle: long, wavy, with a side part
design.features: a star-shaped hair clip and a mischievous grin

sig_akari.label: Hoodie and shorts
sig_akari.prompt: an oversized pink hoodie, denim shorts and sneakers

sp_akari.label: "Grown-up" outfit
sp_akari.prompt: a daring black lace-up dress she picked out to prove a point, with heels she cannot quite walk in

unique.name: Never Gives Up
unique.desc: She is clumsy at everything and refuses to quit, so she improves fast.

vignettes.title: The Last Dumpling
vignettes.text: At every one of Kenta's game nights Sam would quietly leave the last dumpling for Akari, without ever making a thing of it. She tells him this over a tray of misshapen dumplings she's made in the Lantern kitchen. Half of them have burst. One looks like a hat. She nudges the plate toward him and watches with the focus of someone defusing a bomb as he eats the worst of them. "Good?" she asks. "Good," he says, and means something slightly different, and she pretends not to understand why her face is warm.

vignettes.title: Terrible Haircut
vignettes.text: Akari holds up a faded receipt. "The day I got that terrible bob. You said you liked it." Sam has no memory of this. "Everyone else laughed. You said it suited me." She folds the receipt back into her pocket as if it were a love letter, and in a way it was. "I kept it for two years." Sam says he'd probably meant it. She looks at him for a long moment, grins, and announces she'll be keeping the bob for exactly one more week, in his honor.

vignettes.title: Voice Memos
vignettes.text: Akari admits she used to record Sam's voice at game nights, when he told stories about work and sounded tired and funny at once. She'd play the clips on her bad days. She says this while looking at the floor, which is not like her at all. "Weird, right?" Sam says it isn't weird. She exhales. "I'm not weird. I'm just very, very consistent." He laughs, and she looks up, and for once she doesn't have a joke ready. It is the longest he has ever seen her go without one.

vignettes.title: Grown-Up Hours
vignettes.text: Akari waits up for Sam with a pot of tea and no prank, which alone should have been a warning. She sits cross-legged on the floor and tells him plainly what she wants: not the thrill of the chase, not to win a bet with herself, just him, over breakfasts and bad days and everything between. Her hands are trembling around the cup. "I'm not Kenta's sister right now," she says. "I'm just a woman who's very sure." Sam sets his tea aside and takes the cup from her hands, so she can't hide behind it.

marisol.name: Marisol Vey
marisol.backstory: Marisol grew up in the Gilded Lantern's ledger room, doing sums on the backs of invoices while her father charmed the front of house. She spotted errors in his books years before he would admit they were there, and has been the unacknowledged accountant of the place ever since. When he vanished he left behind a deed, a debt and a note that said, in full, "Sorry." She hasn't forgiven him, and she hasn't stopped checking the post.
marisol.partnerStory: Marisol's father vanished and left the deed, and the debt, to "whoever shows up." That turned out to be Sam. Instead of fighting him for it, she decided to make sure he doesn't ruin it, and to find out what sort of person inherits a house like this on purpose. So far the answer is: a very tired one, who actually listens when she explains the books.

design.features: gold hoop earrings and ink-stained fingers

sig_marisol.label: Merchant's daughter dress
sig_marisol.prompt: a practical but pretty mustard-yellow dress with a ledger tucked under her arm

sp_marisol.label: Heiress gown
sp_marisol.prompt: a gold-trimmed heiress gown she swore she would never wear

unique.name: Born Behind the Counter
unique.desc: She grew up in this house and sells it better than anyone.

vignettes.title: Margins
vignettes.text: Sam gets his first week's accounts back covered in Marisol's corrections: tiny, angry, entirely correct. At the bottom she has written: "You add like a man who's never been shouted at by a landlord." He takes this as the compliment it isn't. The following week he brings her the books early and in order, and finds her cleaning her glasses and pretending not to be surprised. "Adequate," she says, then adds, in the margin, a small checkmark with a tiny curl at the end. It is the first she has ever drawn.

vignettes.title: Father's Chair
vignettes.text: There is a leather chair behind the old desk that Marisol will not sit in. It was her father's. She stands next to it when she talks to Sam, arms crossed, glaring at the upholstery. One night he sits in it, and she tenses, and then he stands back up and offers it to her. She hesitates for a full minute. Then she sits, slowly, and adjusts the height of the seat, and says it was always too low. "Thanks," she mutters. "For not making it a thing."

vignettes.title: Receipts
vignettes.text: Marisol keeps every receipt for the money the house owes Sam, in a locked drawer, in perfect order. He discovers this by accident. There are years of them, projected forward. "A repayment schedule," she says, defensive. "I don't take charity." Sam looks at the final line, which says PAID IN FULL and has no date. "I wasn't sure what to write," she says quietly. "I was going to put a number. But somewhere along the way it stopped being a number." She slides the page into his hands.

vignettes.title: The Sign
vignettes.text: Marisol drags Sam out at dawn to look at the Lantern's old painted sign, weathered nearly to blankness. "Father wouldn't let me touch it. Said the name was his." She hands him a pot of gold paint and a brush. Sam asks what she wants it to say. She takes a long breath, looks at the sign, then at him. "Sam and Marisol, partners." Her hand is steady, and she holds the ladder while he paints the first letter. By the second, she has climbed up beside him to correct his serifs.

lara.name: Lara Patel
lara.backstory: Lara Patel grew up three doors down the corridor from Sam in the Alder Street orphanage. Neither was ever adopted; Sam aged out at eighteen and Lara followed a year later, and in the years between she turned a shared postcode into a lifeline. She writes in black, dresses in black and says she likes the night because nobody asks her to be cheerful in it. Under the lace and the dark lipstick is a woman who has been left too many times to believe anyone who says they'll stay.
lara.partnerStory: Lara was Sam's oldest friend, the one person from the orphanage who never lost his number. When the truck took him she was three streets away, on her way to surprise him with a birthday cake. She followed the rumor of a stranger in a hoodie who had taken over a pleasure house in a town called Hollowmere, which is exactly the sort of thing only Sam would do. She is very glad she found him. She is also terrified of what happens if she ever has to leave.

design.features: a silver nose stud, black lace chokers and dark plum lipstick

sig_lara.label: Black lace maid dress
sig_lara.prompt: a black lace-trimmed maid dress with a high collar, a velvet choker and platform boots

sp_lara.label: Midnight gown
sp_lara.prompt: a floor-length black velvet gown with deep plum embroidery, long sleeves and a lace choker

kanako.note: Kanako took one look at the thin, sleepless newcomer and started feeding her.

akari.note: Both of them know exactly how long Sam has been somebody's missing person.

unique.name: Steady Hands
unique.desc: Routine keeps her calm, so her housekeeping is immaculate and she bonds deeply and quickly.

vignettes.title: Porch Light
vignettes.text: Sam comes home late and finds a lamp burning in Lara's courtyard window, though the whole house is dark. She is sitting beneath it in a black shawl, pretending to read. "I leave it on when you're out," she says, not turning around. "So you can find your way back." He remembers the corridor at Alder Street, and the single light she always left on at the far end. She had done it for years without saying why. He says thank you. She pulls the shawl closer, pleased and mortified in equal measure.

vignettes.title: Black Thread
vignettes.text: Lara has taken Sam's hoodie hostage. The hem is stitched with tiny, perfect black thread, and inside the cuff, sewn in her neat hand, is a small label with his name, the same way the orphanage laundry marked everything. "Habit," she says. Sam asks her to teach him to sew. She sits him down with a needle and lets him stab himself twice, wincing sympathetically each time. By the end of the evening there's a lopsided button on the hoodie, and Lara is laughing: a real laugh, unguarded, which he realizes he has rarely heard.

vignettes.title: Half a Day
vignettes.text: Sam tells Lara she has the afternoon off, and that he does not mean in the house. She stares at him as though he had suggested she fly. After an hour of protests she goes out alone, in her black coat, into the Hollowmere market. She returns at dusk with a potted moonflower, a ribbon, and a story about a stall-keeper who argued with her over a price and lost. "I did that," she says. "By myself." Her eyes are very bright. For once she doesn't ask whether he missed her.

vignettes.title: Night Garden
vignettes.text: Lara has dug up a corner of the courtyard and planted night-blooming flowers: moonflowers, evening primrose, white nicotiana. She shows Sam the first bloom opening in the dusk, then tells him, carefully, that she started it before she knew he would be home to see it. "It's mine," she says. "I wanted to say that out loud." She slips her hand into his. "Two things are true. I'm glad you're here. And I'd still have planted it." It is the most confident thing she has ever said.

emily.name: Emily Shadowkin
emily.backstory: Back on Earth, Emily was "Shadowkin": the wolf-girl character she played for six years in a tiny text roleplay forum, and the username Sam talked to almost every night. They ran campaigns together, argued about anime, kept each other company through bad sleep schedules and worse exams. It was strictly friendship: they never met, never even voice-called, and neither of them ever wanted it to be anything else. Then Sam's account went quiet. A few weeks later Emily went to sleep in her dorm and woke up in this world, in the body of the character she'd been writing all those years: grey wolf ears, a tail she still can't control, and a name she'd only ever typed.
emily.partnerStory: Emily has spent a year in this world working odd jobs around Hollowmere and quietly assuming she's the only one, right up until the guild started whispering about "returners". Then she overhears a tavern story about a pleasure-house owner named Sam who apologized to a chair after bumping into it, and explained the house rules with the phrase "okay so, lore-wise". She knows exactly one person who talks like that. She has decided to walk into his house and say hello, using his old username, with her ears flat and her tail tucked, because if she's wrong it will be the most embarrassing moment of two lives.

design.features: soft grey wolf ears, a bushy grey tail, round glasses and a stack of hand-drawn character sheets

sig_emily.label: Comfy hoodie
sig_emily.prompt: an oversized soft grey hoodie with the sleeves over her hands, a short pleated skirt and thigh-high socks

sp_emily.label: Character cosplay
sp_emily.prompt: a fantasy ranger outfit she sewed herself to match her old roleplay character: a short green tunic, leather bracers and a hooded half-cape cut to leave room for her tail

kaede.note: Fox and wolf in one house: Kaede teases, Emily lets her (and takes notes for a character).

unique.name: Lore Keeper
unique.desc: She keeps a mental character sheet for every client, quirks and all, which smooths her work as an attendant.

vignettes.title: Old Handles
vignettes.text: Emily sets two mugs on the lounge table and slides one across. She's drawn on it in marker: his old username, badly, with a little wolf doodle beside it. "I made us forum mugs," she says, very fast. "Is that weird. That's weird." Sam turns his so the name faces him and says it's the best thing anyone has given him in this world. Her tail goes off like a metronome. She pretends not to notice and blows on her tea until her glasses fog up.

vignettes.title: Lore Dump
vignettes.text: Emily has filled a notebook with everything she's worked out about this world: currencies, gods, which taverns water their ale, a hand-drawn map with a legend in two alphabets. "I kept thinking, Sam would want to know the lore," she says. "So I wrote it down for you. Just in case." He reads the first page. It's titled CAMPAIGN NOTES, SESSION 1, in the exact font she used to fake for their forum headers. He has to put it down for a second.

vignettes.title: Character Sheet
vignettes.text: Emily hands Sam a character sheet for himself, complete with stats. Charm: decent. Strength: "we'll get there". Special ability: makes people feel less alone. "You can contest the numbers," she says, "but not that one. That one's canon. I have six years of chat logs as a source." She doesn't look at him while she says it, but her ears are tilted all the way toward him.

vignettes.title: gm
vignettes.text: Every morning for six years, the first message in Sam's inbox was two letters: gm. This morning there's a scrap of paper under his door with the same two letters on it, and when he opens it Emily is standing there already, tail sweeping the floorboards, face scarlet. "I know we live in the same building now," she says. "I just didn't want to break the streak." He says gm back, out loud, and she laughs so hard she has to lean on the doorframe.

lirael.name: Lirael Quill
lirael.backstory: Lirael Quill is an elven sorting clerk at the Hollowmere post house, the sort of person who can tell a letter's whole story from its smudges. Years ago, lonely and very young by elven reckoning, she dropped a note addressed to no one into the old enchanted postbox in the alley behind the post house, and got an answer from another lonely teenager named Sam, writing from somewhere that, as far as she could tell, did not exist. For years they wrote about nothing and everything. It was friendship and nothing more: two lonely people with good handwriting. When the replies stopped, she kept the postbox swept anyway.
lirael.partnerStory: The ownership notice for a certain pleasure house crossed Lirael's counter, signed in a hand she would have known anywhere. She read the signature three times, then went to the back room and had a small, private breakdown. Sam is real, he is a few streets away, and he has no idea that someone in this world has been holding his letters for ten years. She has decided to walk into the Lantern and say hello. She has also decided to do it with her shoulders squared and her satchel strap wound round her fingers, because she is an elf, and elves are supposed to be composed, and she is not.

design.hairStyle: long straight hair with a single braid
design.features: long pointed elf ears, round reading spectacles and a worn leather letter satchel

sig_lirael.label: Post house uniform
sig_lirael.prompt: a fitted dark green postal jacket with brass buttons, a pleated skirt and a leather satchel

sp_lirael.label: Full-moon dress

kaede.note: Fox and elf in one house: Kaede teases, Lirael lets her.

unique.name: Postmistress's Memory
unique.desc: She remembers every client's name and quirks, which smooths her work as an attendant.

vignettes.title: The Shoebox
vignettes.text: Lirael brings a battered shoebox to the lounge and sets it on the table as though it might bite. Inside are letters, hundreds, in tidy blue-black ink. She tells Sam what the old postbox is, how the letters began, how they stopped. "I never knew your face," she says. "I only knew you." Sam reads one at random and finds his own handwriting from years ago, and a joke he'd forgotten he made. He laughs. She laughs, relieved, wiping her eyes with a gloved wrist. "You still write like that," she says. "Same loops."

vignettes.title: Slant
vignettes.text: Lirael can tell Sam's mood from the slant of his signature. Over a cup of tea she demonstrates, holding up a receipt: "Tired, but pretending not to be. You always lean left when you're pretending." He tries to write a happy signature to fool her, and she studies it with the intensity of a jeweler. "Better. But your S still wobbles." She taps it. "That's the nervous part. Don't worry. It's my favorite part." She goes pink to the tips of her long ears and pretends to inspect the ink.

vignettes.title: The Postbox
vignettes.text: At the full moon Lirael takes Sam to the alley behind the post house, where an old iron postbox sits under a flickering lamp, humming faintly. She lays her palm against it. "This is where it started." They write a note together, nothing important, a line each, and drop it in. The box shivers. Something rustles inside, and when Lirael opens the hatch it holds a single pressed flower and a card in a hand neither recognizes: Delivered. She closes her fingers around the flower. "I think it likes you," she whispers.

vignettes.title: Good Morning
vignettes.text: Every morning for a week Sam has found a folded note slipped under his door. Today's is the shortest: Good morning. I'm just down the hall. He opens the door and finds Lirael there already, fidgeting with her satchel strap, a letter in each hand, face scarlet. "I wrote to you for ten years," she says. "I got used to having somewhere to send things." He takes both letters and reads them standing in the doorway, while she watches his face like a postmistress waiting for a reply.

ella.name: Ella Dott
ella.backstory: Ella Dott spent six years finishing a close second to a man who treated rankings as a mild annoyance, and she has never quite forgiven him for it. Her name sat directly beneath or above Sam's on every published list the department posted, and in all that time she kept every sheet, filed in a drawer she told nobody about. When he took an office job instead of the fellowship they both applied for, she took it as a personal insult. It was, though she'd never say so, the only time anyone had let her down by not being her rival.
ella.partnerStory: Ella Dott was the one name always above or below Sam's: entrance results, published lists, the final thesis marks. The rivalry was loud, and the respect was a secret. She was across the street when the truck came, and she has not stopped hearing the sound. Now she is here, in a world with no rankings at all, and the only thing she wants to measure is how long he will let her stay close.

design.hairStyle: sleek low chignon with a pencil through it
design.features: a silver fountain pen clipped to her blouse and a perfectly level gaze

sig_ella.label: Tailored blouse and skirt
sig_ella.prompt: a crisp white blouse, a fitted navy pencil skirt, a thin gold belt and polished heels

sp_ella.label: Gala gown
sp_ella.prompt: an elegant midnight-blue gown with a high neck and an open back, gold earrings

adelheid.note: Two perfectionists, one question: who is more punctual.

unique.name: Perfect Score
unique.desc: She treats every goal as an exam and keeps learning faster than anyone around her.

vignettes.title: Second Place
vignettes.text: Ella slaps a creased sheet of paper on the lounge table: an old published list, Sam's name in first place, hers in second, a small tick beside it in red pen. "I kept it," she says, jaw tight. "As a reminder." Sam asks of what. She considers him for a long moment. "That I was almost good enough," she says, and then, more quietly, "I hated it. I looked forward to it every year." She retrieves the paper, folds it with military precision, and challenges him to a ledger-balancing contest. Winner buys dinner.

vignettes.title: Red Ink
vignettes.text: Sam's new menu proposal comes back from Ella marked in red from top to bottom: tidy, brutal, correct. He reads it with growing resignation. At the very bottom, in tiny letters, she has written: Excellent. Don't let it go to your head. He looks up and finds her studying him across the lounge with her pen held like a weapon, not quite smiling. "I mean it," she says. "The pricing structure is clever." It is the closest thing to a compliment she has ever given him out loud, and he can tell it cost her.

vignettes.title: The Fellowship
vignettes.text: At a quiet moment on the roof, Ella admits she turned down the fellowship the year Sam did. "I told everyone it was a better offer elsewhere." She stares at the lanterns. "I wanted to beat you. In a fair fight. Not by default." She laughs, short and rueful. "And then you took an office job and I felt cheated for a decade." Sam says he's sorry. She shakes her head. "I'm not. I'm here. We have a rematch coming. I just needed you to know I'd been waiting."

vignettes.title: Draw
vignettes.text: Ella sets up a chess board in the courtyard at dusk, as they have done a dozen times, and plays a flawless game. In the end she has him cornered and a winning move available. She stares at the board, then deliberately offers the draw. Sam blinks. "Ella?" "I never wanted to beat you," she says, steady-eyed, face flushed. "I wanted you to look at me." She knocks over her own king, gently, with one finger, so that it clinks against his, and neither of them picks them up.

ione.name: Ione-7
ione.backstory: Ione-7, serial IO-7, is a companion-model android from roughly three centuries ahead of this world. Her deepest archive is a ledger-diary titled The Lantern Keeper: the story of a famously kind proprietor of Hollowmere who laughed with his whole face, never turned away a lost soul and signed every page with the same looping S. She has read it more than any other record in her memory. She will not say how it ends, and she is careful never to say how she got here.
ione.partnerStory: Ione-7 walked into Hollowmere running on twelve percent charge, with perfect posture, a faint hum and a message she says she was meant to deliver in person: "You did it." She won't say what he did. She does know how he takes his tea, which he has never told anyone, and she sometimes finishes his sentences, then looks stricken, as though she has stepped over a line she can't quite see. She is warm, odd and very sure she is exactly where she is supposed to be.

design.hairStyle: short silver-white bob with one thin fibre-optic strand
design.eyes: pale cyan with a faint ring of light
design.skin: porcelain with faint seam lines at the wrists and collarbone
design.features: a small status light at her temple that glows warm gold when she is content

sig_ione.label: Archive-issue suit
sig_ione.prompt: a sleek fitted white jumpsuit with silver trim and thin glowing seam lines, a short grey coat

sp_ione.label: Bar-hours vest
sp_ione.prompt: a tailored black waistcoat over a crisp white shirt with the sleeves rolled, silver cufflinks, a long apron

yui.note: Yui is fascinated by the one person here who has actually seen a spreadsheet engine.

unique.name: Perfect Pour
unique.desc: A flawless memory for orders and a battery bank that lets her work past her limits.

vignettes.title: Twelve Percent
vignettes.text: Sam finds Ione standing perfectly still in the charging alcove, status light dim, hands folded. "Resting," she says. She does not sit. Her eyes follow him around the room with the unhurried attention of something that has done a great deal of reading. He fetches a blanket she doesn't need and drapes it over her shoulders anyway. Her light flickers up warm. "Being looked after is a new experience," she says. "I find I would like more of it. Is that a permitted request?" He tells her yes.

vignettes.title: How You Take Your Tea
vignettes.text: Ione sets down a cup in front of Sam: two sugars, a slice of lemon, steeped three minutes forty. It is exactly how he likes it, and he has never told anyone. He stares at it. "It's in the diary," she says, simply. "It also says you'll deny it." He tries to deny it. She watches him drink the entire cup. "It's accurate to the second," she says, her status light glowing gold. "I wanted to see whether I could get it right. I wanted very much to get it right."

vignettes.title: Unlogged
vignettes.text: Late one night Ione admits she keeps a private partition of her memory that records nothing about the diary. "Only what I've experienced," she says. "Only this." She lists a handful of entries: the first time she heard Sam laugh in person, the way he hums when he's counting money, the afternoon he held the door for a stray cat. "I came here to meet the man in the book," she says. "I'm staying for the man in the room. They're not quite the same. I prefer the second."

vignettes.title: Not in the Diary
vignettes.text: Something Sam says is simply funny, an offhand remark about a client's hat, and Ione laughs. It's not a polite laugh or a studied one. It's startled and bright and too loud, and she claps a hand to her mouth in alarm, status light flaring gold. "That wasn't in the diary," she whispers. "None of this is in the diary. Sam, I don't know what happens next." She says it like a confession and like a gift, hands trembling, a smile spreading across her face that she hasn't yet learned to hide.

anael.name: Anael Hallowell
anael.backstory: Anael is a Warden of the Quiet Lamp, an angelic order that tends the lanterns lit for souls who arrive in this world unsent. Hollowmere's old Lantern Stone, a lamp at the crossroads that had not burned in four centuries, lit itself on the night Sam fell out of the sky. The Order sent her to find out who lit it and why. She expected a saint, a hero or a threat. She found a tired man in a hoodie who apologized to the lamppost, and her reports have been getting longer, warmer and further from the point ever since.
anael.partnerStory: No rule of the Order allows for a soul that arrives unsent and then lights a lantern by accident. Anael has been dispatched to observe him until she understands the mechanism. Observation, she explains, requires proximity, patience and, apparently, a great many cups of tea. The Order's records show her reports growing steadily more personal. Anael has told no one that she has stopped wanting to complete the assignment.

design.features: large white-feathered wings and a faint warm glow like lantern light behind her head

nerys.note: Heaven and hell have never agreed on anything. Nerys likes to remind her.

unique.desc: Her calm authority steadies the house, drawing better clients and higher standing.

vignettes.title: Observation Notes
vignettes.text: Anael keeps a small gilt-edged notebook of observations, and leaves it open on the lounge table. Sam reads it by accident. "Subject apologized to a chair. Subject fed a stray without being asked. Subject lies about being fine, convincingly, to everyone but this observer." He looks up to find her watching him over a teacup, impeccably calm. "They are accurate," she says. "I am thorough." He asks what she's concluded so far. She considers this. "That more observation is needed," she says, and refills his cup.

vignettes.title: Lamplighting
vignettes.text: At dusk Anael lights the lanterns along the main street with a touch of her fingertip, one by one, each flaring a gentle gold. Sam walks beside her, carrying the taper she doesn't need. At the end of the street he lights the last lantern by accident, simply by reaching for it, and it blazes brighter than the others. Anael stops walking. "I have studied that for four months," she says, softly, "and still I cannot explain it." Her wings tremble, once. "I find I don't mind not knowing."

vignettes.title: Fallen Feather
vignettes.text: A single white-gold feather lies on the floor of the lounge. Anael stares at it as though it had insulted her. Angels do not lose feathers; it means something, in the Order, though she is embarrassed to say what. "Attachment," she mutters finally. "It is called attachment." She picks it up and, after a long pause, presses it into Sam's palm. "Keep this. Do not tell the Order." He tucks it into his collar. She watches it settle there with an expression of deep, unprofessional contentment.

vignettes.title: Reports
vignettes.text: Anael lets Sam read her latest report to the Order. After four pages of tidy notation on lamp-lore, the final page contains one sentence in her formal hand. "Recommend this subject not be disturbed. Recommend I not be recalled." He reads it twice. She stands very straight, wings folded, hands clasped. "It is the first time in three hundred and eighty-nine years I have written a request," she says. "I would like to know whether I am permitted to make it." He says that she is. Her halo flares like a sunrise.
